title: The DEXA-PSYCH trial
text:
The DEXA-PSYCH trial is an investigator-initiated, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group superiority trial. Three-hundred participants meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe depression were be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to 1 week of either dexamethasone or placebo as add-on treatment to treatment as usual.


Per date: 2026-11-02

Enrollment: Done. 300 participants randomized.
Completion: Main trial (up to day 28 visit) is complete. Six-month follow-up is on-going.

For further details, see the timeline.



Depression is one of the leading causes of years lived with disability, globally. The effects of current pharmacological treatments are small-to-moderate and often delayed by weeks. Immunological disturbances have been associated with depression and meta-analyses have suggested that anti-inflammatory agents have moderate-to-large anti-depressant effects. The largest effects were reported for glucocorticoids. However, previous trials were too small to legitimize standard use of glucocorticoids as add-on treatment in depression.



The purpose of the DEXA-PSYCH trial was to investigate the effect and safety of short-term, oral dexamethasone compared to placebo as add-on therapy in moderate-to-severe depression.



All pre-specified and pre-programmed trial results are available in Tables, Listings and Figures (TLF) book here. (Link will contain trial results upon publication of the primary)
For further details see the trial results page



The primary publication of the DEXA-PSYCH trial is available here (Link will go live upon publication of the primary paper.) For more information on publications see here.



The DEXA-PSYCH trial has EU Trial registration number 2022-501428-45-00 with WHO universal Trial Identifier U1111-1280-7614.
The Trial protocol is available here in its latest version and an earlier version is presented in Rømer et al (2025)



The Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) was archived and locked in a persistent and immutable Zenodo DOI prior to unblinding of the randomization list. The time of unblinding coincides with locking of the database and is called database lock (DBL).



All code to produce the statistical analyses is openly shared on the DEXA-PSYCH GitHub repository.
Analyses were programmed with dummy treatment-group identifiers, and the code was archived before unblinding. The primary analysis of the primary endpoint was independently parallel programmed by two separate statisticians.
The README file describes the structure and contents of the code base.
The Change log describes the evolution and maintenance of the code base and new releases of trial results.



The key timeline for the main trial is as follows:

202X-mmm: Application for function
202X-mmm: Approval by medical agency
2023-01-13: First patient randomized
yyyy-mm-dd: Last version of the protocol (version 1.4) accepted by XX and published
2026-10-12: Day-28 visit of the last patient
2026-10-19: Final GCP assessment
2026-10-20: Statistical analysis plan locked in Zenodo DOI
2026-10-21: Database locked, Statistical analysis code finalized and locked in Zenodo DOI
2026-10-22: Randomization list received: unblinding of statisticians, principal investigator and selected sub-investigators
2026-10-23: All Pre-specified analyses run and results archived in immutable Zenodo DOI
2026-mm-dd: Primary publication published

As of October 2026 2 assessors remain unblined to collect 6-month follow-up data. The last follow-up data is expected to be collected March 2027.

title: Trial Results
text:
The code in this repository produces two Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLF) books; a primary publication version and a clinical trial report (CTR) version. All outcomes are reported from day 0 to day 28. Long term follow-up (until 6 months after baseline) will be presented separately.

Primary Publication: This version documents all summaries and statistical analyses for safety and efficacy endpoints presented in the primary publication as documented in the SAP and trial protocol. This version is archived in a Zenodo DOI here.
Clinical Trial Protocol (CTR): This version includes all content reported in the primary publication version but also presents results for additional secondary outcomes. Contents for the secondary outcomes will be released upon publication of secondary papers presenting the additional secondary outcomes. This version of the TLF-book is archived in a Zenodo DOI here.

The primary publication TLF-book is available here although it is password-protected for reviewer access until the primary publication is published.

title: About
text:
The DEXA-PSYCH trial was conducted at the Copenhagen Research Centre for Biological and Precision Psychiatry, Mental Health Centre Copenhagen, Copenhagen University Hospital—Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg, Copenhagen, Denmark.
The trial was lead by sponsor and principal investigator Michael Eriksen Benros

title: About
text:
Funding
The DEXA-PSYCH trial was funded by

An unrestricted research grant for investigator-initiated trials with a non-commercial focus awarded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation (grant number NNF21OC0072020)
Mental Health Services in the Capital Region of Denmark

The funders had no role in the design or conduct of the trial, in the analysis or interpretation of data, or in the communication of trial results.

title: About
text:
Approval
The conduct of the trial was approved by the Danish Medicines Agency, the Medical Research Ethics Committee, and the Capital Region Knowledge Center for Data Compliance.
All participants provided written informed consent.
